claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\) be the real regular-octagonal Banach plane
\[
N(u,v)=\max\left\{|u|,|v|,\frac{|u|+|v|}{\sqrt2}\right\}.
\]
Let
\[
J(X)=\sup_{x,y\in S_X}\min\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\}.
\]
Then \(J(X)=\sqrt2\), and
\[
\min\{N(x+y),N(x-y)\}=\sqrt2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
y=\pm Qx,
\]
where \(Q(u,v)=(-v,u)\). Consequently every James-extremizing pair satisfies
\[
N(x+y)=N(x-y)=\sqrt2.
\]
Thus the complete equality set consists exactly of Euclidean quarter-turn pairs.

correctness.rationale: After dihedral reduction, four upper-half boundary pieces force one chord below \(\sqrt2\) except for a shared endpoint. On the top edge \(y=(a,1)\), the two extremality conditions are exactly \(a+t\ge0\) and \(a+t\le0\), so \(a=-t\). Direct substitution gives both chord norms \(\sqrt2\).
risks: Specific to real scalars and this regular-octagonal norm.

value.rationale: The regular octagon is a canonical non-Hilbert plane with the minimal James constant. Classifying every maximizer is a natural structural refinement of the known value: it shows the extremal relation is exactly quarter-turn rotation and forces every extremizer to be isosceles.
risks: This is a complete benchmark classification for one norm, not a family-wide theorem.
